name: watch.process
description: Subscribe to a process's exit, or with `descendants: true` to every spawn and exit in its process tree. Auto-cancels when the process exits, or with `descendants` when every tracked process has exited.

descendants.description: When true, also report descendants. Existing descendants are emitted as `spawned` right after subscribing, so none are missed between `process.start` and this call. The root itself never gets a `spawned` event. Polled every 250 ms: a child that lives less than that may be missed, including an app that crashes on launch.

x-event-schema.description: One `exited` EVENT for the root, then auto-cancel. With `descendants: true`, `spawned` and `exited` EVENTs for every tracked process, then auto-cancel once all have exited. If the root has already exited at subscribe, the agent emits `exited` for it (no `exit_code`), then `spawned` for each live orphan, and auto-cancels at once when there are none.

kind.description: `spawned` when a descendant is first seen; `exited` when a tracked process exits.

image.description: Executable name, as in `process.list`. Present on `spawned`.

exit_code.description: Exit code (or the value passed to TerminateProcess). Present on `exited` when the agent held a handle to the process in time.

x-implementations.name: register_wait_for_single_object
x-implementations.description: Win32 `OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE)` + `RegisterWaitForSingleObject` (NT 5+) — async exit notification on a thread-pool callback. Calls back to the agent's event-emitter when the process signals.

x-implementations.name: wait_thread
x-implementations.description: Dedicated thread + `WaitForSingleObject(hProcess, INFINITE)` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x where RegisterWaitForSingleObject is unavailable.

x-implementations.name: toolhelp_poll
x-implementations.description: Descendant tracking for `descendants: true`. `CreateToolhelp32Snapshot` every 250 ms, diffed against the tracked set. New children of tracked processes emit `spawned`, after the same creation-time pid-reuse check as `process.tree`. A `SYNCHRONIZE` handle is opened on each new process for its exit code.

x-implementations.name: toolhelp_poll_dll
x-implementations.description: The same poll with Toolhelp resolved at runtime (Windows 9x and 2000+). Absent on NT 4.

windows-modern.description: RegisterWaitForSingleObject for the root's exit. `descendants: true` selects toolhelp_poll for the tree; the exit-wait entry serves `descendants: false`. These are not a fallback chain for each other.

windows-classic.description: RegisterWaitForSingleObject on NT 5+, dedicated wait thread on NT 4 / 9x, for `descendants: false`. `descendants: true` selects toolhelp_poll_dll. On NT 4, where Toolhelp is missing, the verb stays advertised and `descendants: true` returns `ERR not_supported` with a `reason` naming `descendants`; that code normally means a whole verb is unavailable and is used here for one argument.
